dedupe_keys.name: colouring britain open crowdsourced building attribute data for britain

description: Colouring Britain is an open knowledge platform that collects and shares attribute data on every building in Britain, run from Loughborough University with support from the University of Cambridge and built on the Colouring Cities platform first developed for Colouring London. It is described as a research-led free public resource built collectively by academia, communities, government, industry and the third sector, and its data categories are location, land use and ownership, form and size, construction and design, age and history, planning and conservation, lifecycle and circularity, energy and retrofit, green and water infrastructure context, urban infrastructure context, disaster management and community. Coverage: buildings across Great Britain, with completeness varying by place and attribute. Access: interactive map and editor with attribute downloads as data extracts; the platform code is open. Licence: data under the Open Database Licence, code under GPL-3.0; free. Caveats: extracts carry attributes without building footprint geometry, which comes from mapping agency data under its own terms, and crowdsourced values need checking against sources. Simulation uses are building age, material and use attributes for stock, retrofit and hazard exposure models and for urban digital twins. Related records: Colouring Dresden, the sister platform for Germany, and the England listed buildings data.
